arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Global-Tech advocates for a purposeful and culpable test for inducement.
SEB advocates for a standard that includes willful blindness.
Justice Scalia questioned why a company would not disclose reverse-engineering details.
Justice Alito asked if a client refusing to know avoids liability.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: Global-Tech Appliances and SEB S.A. disagree on the mental state required for patent inducement. Global-Tech argues actual knowledge is necessary. SEB argues deliberate ignorance suffices.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: Global-Tech wants the Court to require actual knowledge of a specific patent.
SEB wants the Court to accept willful blindness as sufficient knowledge.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: Global-Tech argues that only actual knowledge of a specific patent creates liability.
SEB argues that deliberately avoiding information about a patent creates liability.
